In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of SACK is better than Reno and Tahoe only under the assumption of independent losses and when the losses are not too severe.
under losses that occur in the Internet, SACK is the best of the three versions of TCP, Tahoe is second best and Reno is the worst.
SACK is the best choice for TCP implementations, provided that the losses are independent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the latency of SACK is similar to Tahoe and Reno, but the throughput is better than both of them under independent losses and similar to Tahoe under correlated losses.
SACK can perform well only if the loss patterns are independent and that it is not clear whether SACK is the best choice in the current Internet.
in the presence of independent losses SACK is the best choice and in the presence of correlated losses Tahoe is the best choice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TCP Reno performs the worst among these three TCP variants and the performance of SACK depends strongly on how losses are distributed.

TCP Tahoe is still a viable alternative to Reno and SACK in the presence of losses and the performance of TCP Reno is not significantly better than that of TCP Tahoe in the presence of the losses that are typical in the Internet.
the choice of TCP variant should not be based on the throughput alone, but should also take into account the transfer times.
